sentences.text: Hello, Andrew.
Andrew.
Hi, Brian.
How you doing?
I'm good.
Are you?
Yeah, I'm good, thank you.
Sorry I'm a couple of minutes late.
Easter holiday so I've got children everywhere.
Oh, no worries.
Yeah, it starts with us next week.
Hey, I see Fireflies.
Note taker was taking the call.
Oh yeah?
Did it get in before me?
Okay, so you're taking notes with Fireflies, right?
I am, yeah.
Is that an issue?
I can turn it off if you don't want it.
No, it's, it's okay with me.
I mean, it's okay.
Hey, good, we have a call because I received quite a lot of emails from you and.
Yeah, well, to be quite honest, I'm spammed to death with all kinds of emails all day.
Like people who can double my, my revenue, have a thousand appointments in two weeks, those kind of emails, but also your email.
But at least you put in some effort.
I saw.
So that's good.
Hey, and the reason I contacted you is that we, my partner, my business partner and I are in the process like, okay, what are we going to do with our company in about three, four years?
We're doing it now for about almost 10 years.
So what are we going to do in about two, three years or four years?
We haven't decided on the, on, on the term yet but it's so it's more like, okay, are we, are we pulling the plug then?
Are we going to sell it?
Are we going to merge?
Are we going to.
Well there are endless opportunities and then your emails came along and basically you're in the business of, of selling companies.
Right, to other companies.
Yeah.
Happy to give you a little bit of background on us before we get into what it is that you're looking to do.
So we're an M and A advisory and we just work in marketing services.
So all of our clients are either buying or selling marketing agencies.
We work both the buy and the sell side.
Our sell side platform is Agencies Co, which is the marketplace for agency owners to buy and sell.
But we also work on the buy side as capital A as well.

So our clients tend to either be high growth marketing agencies that are looking to acquire other businesses and merge them in or form small groups or we work directly with private equity as well, helping them to find businesses to acquire either as platforms or bolt on.
So yeah, that's us, that's what we do.
Because your scope is UK or European or what's your.
Where do you have most of your potential sellers or buyers?
Yeah, so the majority of what we do is actually in the U.S.
but so we work, we tend to work with a lot of US buyers looking for agencies and they look globally to be fair.
So they tend to buy in the UK or Europe and a little bit so Middle east, like Turkey and Israel and those types of places.
So it's a global business, but we're based in the UK and most of our team is either UK or New York, Los Angeles, San Francisco.
So.
Okay.
Hey, and can you talk me through a little bit your approach?
So, because obviously I've, I sent you the deck I have.
I think it matches about 95 of the questions you ask in your, in your survey or you know, what I have had to fill in.
Yeah, the question.
Yeah, maybe, maybe you should have a look at your terms and conditions because it's pretty steep for an initial contact.
But I'll leave that to you.
So on the website.
Yeah, the website covers companies that fill in an application form to list.
I mean it is what it is, but it is actually an agreement for us to list their business and then we act as their broker for the business and we take a percentage on the deal closing.
So those terms and conditions are just really to cover that process.
Okay, yeah, I understand, but it's more like the initial contact.
You basically sign a contract in which you hand over the keys to you and say, sell my company, which is obviously your business, but I'm not used to that in the first context.
So that's why I requested a call first.
So what percentage percentage do you take?
Just so we take 5% on the transaction.
Most of the clients that we have tend to be sort of sub 10 million deals.
So it's.
We, we do work on, on large contracts as well, so it kind of depends.
But the 5% tends to cover pretty much 99 of what we do.
Okay.
Okay, cool.
So did you have a chance to look at my, the, the thing?
Let me just find it because I didn't see it in any of the initial emails.
Okay.
Yeah, the Red Snap BV thing.
Yeah, I did have a look at it.
Yeah.
Okay.
So it's one of my BVs.
It's a pretty small company, as you see.
However, it's more like, well, is it sellable, do you think, or do I need to find another way?
Yeah.
So interestingly, a lot of people do ask me that, is my company sellable if it's below 1 million EBITDA.
So there's kind of a sweet spot between 1 and 5 million revenue where there's a lot of buyers but also when we sell smaller agencies, the sub 1 million revenue, we do get a lot of activity.
So for instance, we had a company that we sold in Los Angeles last year which had 45 signed MBAs in the first 24 hours of US marketing it.
So there is a lot of activity around small agencies as well.
We've got an agency listed in Switzerland that has also had a lot of interest.
And it's tiny.
I mean, it's really small.
It's just one lady who's been a freelancer.
So the smaller companies also do get a lot of activity.
Okay.
It's necessarily a problem.
And you're in Amsterdam, right?
Yeah, very near Amsterdam, yes.
Which is a, you know, even for Americans, they'll have heard of it and so they'll feel confident that it's a good place to buy agencies in.
So my feeling is we'll probably get quite a lot of interest.
Okay, so how would the process work then?
So let's assume I fill it in or may you have already 95% of the.
Of the information.
But what happens then?
Yeah, so there's a couple of different ways you can go.
So it depends.
Usually the smaller businesses would choose one of the first two ways.
So if you want us to list you on the agency's platform, we do kind of a light valuation and we help you with the IM to get it to a point where it's good.
And then we post it not just on our website, but also it goes out to the 20,000 people on our mailing list.
And that, that is how we got those initial 45 signed NDAs for the smaller agency in Los Angeles.
And that's usually enough.
We had actually for that one guy who was selling his business in la, we got five offers on the table.
So this is the, the cheapest way to go.
It's low commitment, but it can get really good results.
What we don't do is we don't build a big list of potential buyers and go out and market every single day.
So it's the, the easiest way to do it.
If you've got a good business, then it's a, it's a good opportunity to get in front of 20,000 people plus because we get visits to the website as well, it's two and a half thousand dollars.
But like I say, we help you with that valuation to get the valuation right.
And also in preparation for the im, which is the deck that you sent us, it will need a few tweaks, but we'll help you get that sorted as well.
So that's the easiest way to do it, the cheapest option.

And then there's a slightly sort of pricier version of that where we do a full valuation process, which is where we, we spend about a week or so, we go through all of the financials of the business, we prepare a valuation document, and that's 9850.
Basically, if you're kind of a bit more serious about getting it sold quickly, that's probably the better way to go for your size of business.
And then we have something that's 25,000 that I would advise is probably not the right, the right route for you.
So it's one of those two options, really.
Okay, so you pay $2,500 and then when it is sold, you get 5% of the transaction value.
Yeah.
And that you, you, that's net of that fee that you've paid.
So.
One second, I've got a delivery man.
The dog's going nuts.
So, yeah, so that two and a half thousand that you've paid already, that's if we get any win fees at the end of selling, then it's net of that two and a half thousand.
So say our fee was 20,000, it would be 17 and a half.
Okay, I understand.
Okay, I understand.
So can you tell me a little bit about your win rates or the likability of your.
How many percent is actually being sold or what's your success rate?
Success rate is about 1 in 3 to, to get over the line, which is around standard in the industry.
The difference with us is that actually we continue to list and sell.
Sorry, one second, I've got delivery guy.
Okay.
Sorry, Brian.
Yeah, so it's about one in three, but we continue to work on the deals until we get them closed.
So the reason why it's not 100% is because quite often we have clients that aren't sure that they want to sell.
They, they aren't sure what the valuation of the business is.
And we pretty much get offers on every single business.
So you will get offers, but it's down to you then whether you want to, whether you want to take it.
But the market has spoken.
In simple terms, it really is that a business can only generate offers that the market will bear.
So that's kind of the bottom line.
And I think, you know, some of our clients want to see what their company is worth, but they don't ultimately accept offers in the end.
So it's not really that you won't get offers.
You will get them.
Okay.
Okay, cool.
Hey, and how Many.
How many agencies?
I mean do you have activities in the Netherlands?
So we do mainland Europe as well.
We are active there.
Yeah.
I mean we've got an agency listed in Paris.
I'm not sure about the Netherlands currently, but we've got agencies in Paris, agencies in Israel, agencies in Turkey, in Germany.
We've bought agencies in Germany and Belgium.
So we're actively, you know, working across borders.
Okay.

No, it's more like, I mean if somebody buys my company, he probably, I mean, I understand the roll up structure that he wants to buy extra EBITDA or revenue or whatever or my clients, but it's more like how do they get the synergy if I'm bought by an LA company, for example?
Well, it's, it's usually then they're not looking entirely for synergies.
If they were, if you were to be bought by an American company, they would be looking for geography.
You know, they're looking for reach and new markets.
The Netherlands is obviously, you know, a western country is very creative.
It's very, you know, it's well known.
It's not like one of the East European countries.
So we would expect a ton of activity and they would be buying for reach, you know, your reach into Europe and European brands.
So that's my feeling on that.
I don't, don't know whether they would necessarily look for loads of cost savings in that instance.
It would be more that they would be able to do more.
And another thing that we are seeing is offshoring as well from the U.S.
so you know, Europe is cheaper salaries.
In LA, for instance, you can hire a kid who's just come out of university and they want like $250,000 on day one.
So you can get high levels of skill in Europe for less.
And America is doing that a lot as well, you know, so there's going to be a good opportunity I think for American buyers.
Okay.
Okay, cool.
Well, that was basically what I wanted to know.
Let me.
So probably it's still necessary if I fill in that whole thing right or not or is it not necessary anymore?
Well, it is necessary.
It depends which route you want to go.
So obviously we're talking about two routes.
One is where we do it with you, which is the two and a half thousand we will need to extract all of that information from you.
But I will get my team to look at your deck that you sent over and if we don't need anything extra then, then that's fine.
We can create the listing.
But it is the easiest way for us to get started is just.
I mean, we're going to have to ask you those questions anyway, so.
Okay.
Okay.
Hey, I'm talking to.
I've got a management meeting with my partner tomorrow, so I will ask if he's okay with the route to go.
And then how do I contact you?
Just by email or how do I.
So what I'll do, Brian, is after this call, I'll send you a summary of what we discussed.
And you've got.
You'll have that information in an email so you can speak to your partner and.
And decide whether it's the route to go forward with.
And so, yeah, we can discuss on email.
And the next steps are to sign an engagement letter and book in a kickoff call.
And then we'll just deep dive into the business so that we really understand what the opportunity is.
Because what we like to do is when we get interest, we don't just, you know, give you a warm lead and say, this is the buyer.
We actually act on your behalf as well.
We'll screen the potential buyers, particularly if it's somebody we've never spoken to before or we haven't spoken to them in the last three months.
We'll have a call with them.
We'll take them through the opportunity.
So we really want to get them excited before we book a call with you, and then they'll be hot, ready to go, and they'll just have a bunch of questions.
But for you, it's really more about chemistry.
Is this a good person to take over your agency?
Is there a good fit culturally, those sorts of things for you?
Cool.
All right, I'll send over in an email.
We can get started.
Thank you very much for your time.
No worries.
Nice to meet you, Brian.
Enjoy the rest of your day.
Bye.

summary.overview: The Initial Sales Consultation meeting between Brian van Wachem from RedSnap BV and Andrew Day from Capital A focused on exploring potential options for RedSnap's future in the next few years. Andrew introduced Capital A as an M&A advisory specialized in marketing services, highlighting their global operations primarily centered in the US. They discussed RedSnap's valuation and marketability, with Andrew assuring Brian that even smaller agencies can attract interest, citing a successful example from LA. Two primary selling options were presented: a light valuation for $2,500 plus a 5% commission or a full valuation for $9,850, both aimed to facilitate RedSnap's market entry, especially considering its favorable location in Amsterdam. The conversation also covered the success rates of Capital A's transactions, with a one-in-three success rate being the industry standard. As next steps, Brian is to consult with his business partner regarding the selling options, while Andrew will send a summary of their discussion and prepare an engagement letter if Brian decides to proceed.
summary.short_summary: Brian van Wachem from RedSnap BV and Andrew Day from Capital A met to discuss RedSnap's future options, focusing on valuation and marketability. Capital A, an M&A advisory firm specializing in marketing services, highlighted their global presence with a strong focus on the US market. They presented two selling options for RedSnap: a light valuation costing $2,500 plus a 5% commission and a full valuation for $9,850. Both options are designed to facilitate RedSnap's entry into the market, particularly due to its favorable location in Amsterdam. Andrew assured Brian that smaller agencies can attract interest, referencing a successful case from Los Angeles. They also discussed Capital A's industry-standard success rate of one-in-three transactions. Brian plans to consult with his business partner regarding the selling options, and Andrew will provide a summary of their discussion and prepare an engagement letter if Brian chooses to proceed.
